{{Short description|Set of mathematical inequalities}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Newton inequalities''' refer to a set of [[Inequality (mathematics)|mathematical inequalities]] related to [[Series (mathematics)|mathematical series]]. These inequalities are named after [[Isaac Newton]] who proved the theorem in 1707.<ref>{{cite book |last=Newton |first=Isaac |title=Arithmetica universalis: sive de compositione et resolutione arithmetica liber |year=1707}}</ref> Suppose ''a''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;''a''<sub>2</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''a''<sub>''n''</sub> are non-negative [[real number]]s and let <math>e_k</math> denote the ''k''th [[elementary symmetric polynomial]] in ''a''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;''a''<sub>2</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''a''<sub>''n''</sub>.  Then the '''elementary symmetric means''', given by

:<math>S_k = \frac{e_k}{\binom{n}{k}},</math>

satisfy the [[inequality (mathematics)|inequality]]

:<math>S_{k-1}S_{k+1} \le S_k^2.</math>

Equality holds [[if and only if]] all the numbers ''a''<sub>''i''</sub> are equal. 

It can be seen that ''S''<sub>1</sub> is the [[arithmetic mean]], and ''S''<sub>''n''</sub> is the ''n''-th power of the [[geometric mean]].
